column1: # The rules of ZAP's baseline scan that web-console/zap lets pass, each with
# its reason. A line is the rule's number, a tab, IGNORE, a tab and the
# reason, which has no tab in it (zap-baseline.py reads the file with
# that format: a line with less than three tab-separated parts is
# refused). A rule that warns or fails and is not here fails the test:
# fix the console, or add the rule with the reason it is no fault. The
# rule numbers are those of ZAP's passive scan rules, as the scan's report

column3: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set: admind asks for HSTS only when it serves a certificate an authority signed, since HSTS would keep a browser from passing the one-time warning for the machine's own certificate (ADR 0514)

Re-examine Cache-control Directives: the console's own files, its page, scripts and styles, are the same for every visitor and hold nothing of anyone's; they go out no-cache with an ETag, so that a browser asks again before each use and sees an update at once, and every answer of the API is no-store (admind(8))

Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments: the comments are those of the console's own scripts, whose source is published; words such as user, admin or password in them say what the code does and give away nothing the repository does not
Non-Storable Content, Storable and Cacheable Content: a note on how each answer may be kept, which is as 10015 says: no-store for the API, no-cache with an ETag for the console's own files
Modern Web Application: a note that the page is drawn by its scripts, which ZAP's AJAX spider would follow; the baseline scan only watches, and the browser tests of web-console drive every page
